documents.title: On the cohomology groups of an associative algebra

conventions: Fraktur capitals are written with \mathfrak (e.g. \mathfrak{A}, \mathfrak{P}); Greek letters are kept.
Brace evaluation f\{a_1, \dots, a_m\} and the operations a * f, f * a are kept as printed.
The module action is written a \cdot u and u \cdot a; the Kronecker product is written \times.
Footnotes are appended after the paragraph that cites them, prefixed [Footnote n].

foundations.justification: The article uses sets, mappings, injectivity and surjectivity as elementary background.
foundations.evidence: Printed p. 59 (PDF p. 3) introduces linear mappings and their spaces without defining the underlying set/function notions; p. 64 (PDF p. 8) uses homomorphisms onto an algebra.

foundations.justification: Degrees, finite indices and alternating signs are ordinary arithmetic, not replacements for the cohomology construction.
foundations.evidence: Definition 2.1, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 3), indexes the displayed coboundary formula by m and i and uses powers of -1.

foundations.justification: The ground field is arbitrary; do not assume characteristic zero, perfection or algebraic closure.
foundations.evidence: Section 1 first sentence, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 3), places the associative algebra over an arbitrary field Phi.

foundations.justification: Module K P and Module K A encode vector spaces over the ground field K. They do not impose a unit action by A.
foundations.evidence: Printed p. 59 (PDF p. 3) calls P a linear space over Phi and treats the space underlying A as known. Footnote 4 refers ordinary one-sided modules to Jacobson, The Theory of Rings (1943), pp. 14–16.

foundations.notion: Associative algebras without an assumed identity
foundations.justification: Use NonUnitalRing A with Module K A and compatible scalar multiplication. IsScalarTower K A A and SMulCommClass K A A express K-bilinearity of multiplication; no Ring A or Algebra K A assumption is introduced.
foundations.evidence: Section 1, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 3), assumes an associative algebra and does not specify an identity. Printed p. 61 (PDF p. 5) derives an identity only after assuming separability.

foundations.justification: FiniteDimensional K A reflects the finite basis used for the algebra. Do not impose finite dimensionality on every coefficient space P without separate source evidence.
foundations.evidence: Printed p. 59 (PDF p. 3) explicitly chooses a basis a_1,...,a_n of A and describes the Kronecker power as n^m-dimensional. The pilot requirements identify the algebra setting as finite-dimensional.

foundations.justification: Use these elementary linear-algebra notions while retaining the separately authored cochain and twisted-module constructions.
foundations.evidence: Printed p. 59 (PDF p. 3) uses Phi-endomorphisms, citing Jacobson in footnote 5 (pp. 4–5), and defines cochains as linear mappings. Printed p. 60 (PDF p. 4) uses a linear isomorphism between cochain spaces.

foundations.justification: The Kronecker product is elementary background. The source-specific degree-zero convention and positive-degree cochain spaces remain explicit definitions.
foundations.evidence: The second paragraph of section 1, printed p. 59 (PDF p. 3), invokes the Kronecker product of m vector spaces and describes its basis.

foundations.notion: Subspaces, additive subgroups and their quotients
foundations.justification: Use ordinary subspace, subgroup, quotient and kernel machinery. Cocycle, coboundary and cohomology definitions remain source nodes, not imported cohomology objects.
foundations.evidence: Printed p. 60 (PDF p. 4), immediately before and in Definition 2.3, uses subgroups and a quotient group; printed pp. 62–64 (PDF pp. 6–8) uses subspaces, direct sums and kernels.

foundations.justification: Ordinary multiplicative linear maps and subalgebras are background; singularity, segregation and extension equivalence remain authored definitions.
foundations.evidence: Section 6 first paragraph, printed p. 64 (PDF p. 8), assumes algebra homomorphisms and subalgebras while defining extensions, singularity and segregation.

authored.statement_md: [Editorial] Reflexivity requires derivations into every containing algebra to extend to inner derivations there.
authored.description_md: Printed page 689; editorial paraphrase, no Lean declaration or review.

authored.statement_md: [Editorial] In the characteristic-zero semisimple associative setting, every bimodule-valued derivation has form $d(a)=a\cdot p-p\cdot a$.
authored.description_md: Printed page 684; editorial paraphrase, no Lean declaration or review.

authored.statement_md: [Editorial] For associative algebras, reflexivity is characterized by the criterion in `Hochschild1942.Thm_2_2`.
authored.description_md: Printed page 690; editorial paraphrase, no Lean declaration or review.

authored.statement_md: [Editorial] In characteristic zero, semisimple and reflexive algebras coincide.
authored.description_md: Printed page 690; editorial paraphrase, no Lean declaration or review.

authored.statement_md: [Editorial] Separability is equivalent to $H^1(A,P)=0$ for every two-sided $A$-module $P$.
authored.description_md: Printed page 63; editorial paraphrase, no Lean declaration or review. The introduction (p.58, footnote3) identifies earlier Theorems3.4 and3.2 as the predecessor result; this is source-reported context, not an accepted semantic edge.
